title: Reach Beyond Existing Demand
coreMove: Listen to the people near, against, and far outside the market until the common blocker to broader demand becomes visible.
sourcePressure: Move beyond serving current customers by examining the three tiers of noncustomers: soon-to-be, refusing, and unexplored outsiders who reveal common barriers to demand.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating noncustomers as another target segment to market at with louder acquisition tactics.

sourceAnchors.name: three tiers of noncustomers
sourceAnchors.detail: official support names soon-to-be, refusing, and unexplored noncustomers as the framework for reaching beyond existing demand
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The three tiers keep the team from staring only at fans: people about to leave, people refusing, and people never invited each carry a different clue.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: ceramics studio hallway watchers as soon-to-be noncustomers
exampleSpecs.audience: a studio owner whose classes sell out but membership stalls
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the studio serves insiders or opens a path for curious outsiders
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she reads the empty chairs outside the studio as noncustomer evidence, not harmless overflow
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Three coats hang outside the pottery room while every wheel inside is taken

exampleSpecs.domain: clinic families refusing appointments because of surprise bills
exampleSpecs.audience: a healthcare operator serving current patients well but missing nonpatients
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether families seek care early or wait until problems grow
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he sees refusal around bill uncertainty and chooses transparent visit bundles over nicer reminder texts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 9:05 a.m., Antoine hears the third parent ask for the price before the appointment

exampleSpecs.domain: tax help for people ashamed of messy records
exampleSpecs.audience: a solo practitioner tired of competing on credentials
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether informal earners and retirees seek help before deadlines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a caller reveals shared shame across different outsiders, and she creates a first-box appointment instead of an expertise pitch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "What if I bring it in a shoebox?" the caller asks Frida before giving his name

exampleSpecs.domain: fitness demand among shift workers outside studio schedules
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainer whose studio serves committed members but misses shift workers
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether exercise feels possible for people outside normal class times
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he observes a night-shift worker choosing sleep over a 6 p.m. class and sees timing as the blocker
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You unlock the studio at dusk while Pavel watches warehouse badges move the other way

exampleSpecs.domain: school lunch reform for students rejecting the line
exampleSpecs.audience: a nutrition director asking only current healthy eaters what they want
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether better food reaches students who avoid the lunch line
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she traces refusal to social risk and slow lines rather than flavor alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Layla five tasting panels to realize the absent students were the evidence

exampleSpecs.domain: mobile banking refusal among older credit-union members
exampleSpecs.audience: a financial-services manager trying to move service online
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether digital access expands or excludes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts font size is the issue, then hears fraud fear as the common barrier among refusers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The tablet glass reflects James beside a member who keeps both hands on her paper passbook

skillTargets: classify soon-to-be, refusing, and unexplored noncustomers
find shared barriers outside the current customer base
avoid acquisition tactics that ignore why outsiders stay out

tryThisNowSpec: Name one soon-to-be, one refusing, and one unexplored noncustomer, then write the blocker each one would say out loud.
